newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu, PLO go at each other over attack.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu, PLO go at each other over attack.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday demanded that Palestinian President Yasser Arafat help catch Arab gunmen who killed two Jewish settlers, wounded five others and escaped to the PLO-ruled West Bank enclave of Ramallah.
He said the incident posed a test for the Palestinian Authority.

A senior Palestinian official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told Reuters the Palestinian Authority condemned Wednesday's West Bank drive-by shooting and said it was aimed at weakening the PLO's negotiating position vis-a-vis Israel.

Netanyahu, speaking to reporters at a Jerusalem hospital after visiting the wounded, said: "Whoever thinks that the Jewish people can be uprooted from its land, from the heart of the Jewish homeland by these acts of terror should know that we will uproot him."

"The Palestinian Authority now has a test. We expect that they will extradite and first of all help us to arrest these murderers of children, murders of women...We will not let up until we catch them," Netanyahu said.

The Israeli dead were a mother and her 12-year-old son. They and the rest of their family came under fire in their car by Arab gunmen from a passing vehicle near the Jewish settlement of Beit El outside Ramallah, Israeli security sources said.

They said the attackers fled toward Ramallah. Israeli troops in coordination with Palestinian police had entered Ramallah to investigate an abandoned, torched car which fitted the description of the attackers' vehicle, Israel and the PLO said.

Netanyahu, who has been insisting on the right of "hot pursuit" -- chase of wanted persons by Israeli troops into PLO-ruled areas -- at talks on the handover of the West Bank town of Hebron to the PLO, said the only reason Israeli troops did not do so in Wednesday's case was because "engagement" had already been broken by the time troops arrived on the scene.
"If there had been security forces in the area at the time of the incident, they would have done what needed to be done," Netanyahu added.
The PLO official in Gaza self-rule enclave, told Reuters:
"The Palestinian Authority condemns this suspicious act...(it) considers this act directed at this specific time against the Palestinian Authority."

"It is intended to weaken the Palestinian negotiating position and it serves the Israeli side's attempts to escape from carrying out the commitments which have been agreed upon and it helps to cover its playing with the peace process," he added.
The issue of "hot pursuit" has snagged talks PLO-Israel on a Israeli handover of most of the West Bank town of Hebron.

Ramallah with five other West Bank towns was handed to the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) at the end of 1995 under a deal signed more than a year ago between the PLO and Israel's previous government. Hebron was to have been handed over in March, but this was delayed after Moslem militant attacks in Israel.
